text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] KV cache anomalous growth detected in us-west2 - continuous-batching fanout appears to be causing cache blowups. Severity: P1. Multiple workers above 85% GPU memory, OOM risk. Paged on-call.
alice: Ack'd. I'm on-call. pinging @ben (eng-runtime) and @dave (eng-sre).
ben: I'm jumping in. Initial probes show an inflection at ~09:12 UTC coincident with the batch-routing tweak rolled yesterday. KV entries spiked.
ben: quick grep from runtime logs showing counts: 
```
worker=wv-22 kv_cache.entries=1802334 kv_cache.size_bytes=9.2GB batch_inflight=64 qps=120
worker=wv-19 kv_cache.entries=1759011 kv_cache.size_bytes=8.9GB batch_inflight=58
worker=wv-03 kv_cache.entries=42000 kv_cache.size_bytes=200MB batch_inflight=6
```
carla: Confirming from perf-dash. Canary that received max_fanout bump shows 8-12x growth in prefix expansions. Looks like prefix fanout blew out continuous KV caching.
dave: Oncall here. Initiating mitigations: scaling up pool to buy time and isolating hot machines. Will coordinate rolling changes and potential restarts.
erica: Support: we have 8 customers reporting elevated latency, 3 with partial failures. CS triage running; @frank has the customer list.
frank: Impacted customers: cust-psi (heavy batched scoring), cust-lumos, cust-ora, cust-nimble. They've got open tickets. Asked for ETA.
ben: Proposed immediate mitigation: disable continuous batching flag and reduce max_batch_window to limit fanout. Preparing a flag push to runtime manager.
ben: hotfix command to apply (will canary first):
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching":false,"max_batch_window_ms":10,"max_batch_fanout":4}'
```
alice: Applying to us-west2 canary pool now. Monitoring. :eyes:
(10m later)
incident-bot: Canary update: kv_cache growth rate on canary nodes stabilized within normal bounds. 30% latency improvement on canary. No new OOMs.
dave: Rolling this change cluster-wide via orchestrator. Also enabling an immediate arena compaction job on affected nodes to reclaim fragmented CUDA allocations.
ben: Running compaction script: 
```
python tools/arena_compact.py --region us-west2 --dry-run=false
```
ben: Pre-hotfix we saw several CUDA allocation failures in logs, likely allocator fragmentation (pytorch/cuda-malloc path). Example: 
```
E cudaMalloc: out of memory on device 0 while allocating 512MB
stack: at aten::cuda::malloc
```
ben: For medium-term mitigation we should tune PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF and adjust max_split_size_mb + enable more aggressive caching eviction.
carla: Agreed. Follow-ups: 1) revert the last routing param that increased fanout, 2) set lower default max_fanout and max_batch_window, 3) add KV cache growth alarm and auto-safe-mode.
erica: Support update posted to customers. Offering credits to top-affected accounts. Will update when full resolution confirmed.
alice: Status update: mitigations deployed, rolling compaction completed, no new OOMs in last 30m, latency trending to baseline. Downgrading severity to P2 but staying oncall until tomorrow morning. Postmortem owner: ben.
gina: Suggest adding an automated safe-mode: if kv_cache_size_pct > 70% then auto-disable continuous batching and trigger compaction. Also add metric for batch fanout by prefix.
dave: Noted. I'll open infra ticket for automated safe-mode + compaction runbook.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED -> P2] Continuous batching disabled, compaction performed, canary verified. No further immediate customer impact. Postmortem meeting scheduled for tomorrow 16:00 UTC.
alice: Thanks everyone for quick triage and clean rollout. Action items captured in #incidents-tasks. Leaving follow-ups assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml.
